title: Clean and oil the air filter
completeness: Covers opening the airbox, removing, washing, oiling and refitting the foam element, greasing the sealing face and draining the airbox breather. Does not cover the throttle body or intake boot replacement.

required_tools.name: Screwdriver or socket for the side cover bolt

required_parts.name: Spare element
required_parts.purpose: If the old one is torn or worn out.

prerequisites: Non-flammable solvent and dish soap available.
critical_stop_conditions: Dirt found on the clean side of the intake: clean it all out before the engine is started.
Element torn or hardened: replace it, never refit it.
Element not sealing evenly all round: refit it before riding.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and riding hours since the last clean. Plan to clean this filter every race (about 2.5 hours of riding), and after every moto in dusty conditions. Have a second, already oiled element ready if you swap at the track.
verification: Date and hours written down.

steps.title: Clean around the airbox
steps.instruction: Bike cold and upright on a stand. Brush and wipe the area around the left side cover so no grit can fall into the airbox when it opens.
verification: Area around the left side cover clean and dry.

steps.title: Take off the left side cover
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolt and pull the left side cover off.
verification: Side cover off, bolt kept.

steps.title: Lift the element out
steps.instruction: Release the hook of the element setting spring, swing the spring open and lift the foam element out together with its holder. Do not let dirt fall off the element into the clean side of the airbox.
verification: Element and holder out.

steps.title: Clean the airbox and check the breather drain
steps.instruction: Stuff a clean rag into the intake opening so nothing can drop into the engine. Wipe the inside of the airbox clean. Pull out the drain plug at the bottom of the airbox drain hose, let any water, oil mist or dirt run into a container, check the hose is not blocked or split, and refit the plug. Look at the intake side of the boot: dirt there means the element was not sealing, so check the sealing face and the element fit before going on.
verification: Intake covered, airbox wiped, drain emptied.
No dirt on the clean side of the intake.

branches.label: Dirt found past the filter
branches.condition: Dirt on the clean side: clean it out completely before any start, and check the sealing face and element seating closely when refitting.

steps.title: Separate the foam from its frame
steps.instruction: Peel the foam element off its holder, working the holes in the foam gently over the holder tabs so they do not tear.
verification: Foam off its frame, no torn holes or slots.

steps.title: Wash the element
steps.instruction: Wash the foam in a non-flammable cleaning solvent (never gasoline or any low flash point solvent), then wash it again in hot water with dishwashing soap. Squeeze it, do not wring or twist it. Repeat until no dirt comes out, then let it dry completely. Throw away any element that is torn, hardened or coming apart at the seams.
verification: Element clean, fully dry, no tears.

branches.label: Element torn or worn out
branches.condition: Use a new element from here on; do not refit a damaged one.

steps.title: Oil the element
steps.instruction: Put 50 cm³ of foam air filter oil on the inside of the element. Never use engine oil. Put the element in a plastic bag and knead it until the oil is spread evenly through all the foam, then squeeze out the excess without twisting.
verification: Oil even through the whole element, excess squeezed out.

steps.title: Put the foam back on its frame
steps.instruction: Fit the foam back on the holder, hooking each hole in the foam over its holder tab. Do not hook the holes onto the grooves where the setting spring sits.
verification: Every hole or slot on its tab, foam not torn.

steps.title: Grease the sealing face
steps.instruction: Take the rag out of the intake. Spread 1.5–5.5 g of grease on the airbox face where the element seals. This is what stops dust getting past the edge of the filter.
verification: Rag out of the intake, sealing face greased all the way round.

steps.title: Fit the element
steps.instruction: Set the element in the airbox with the projection on the holder in the hole in the housing. Close the setting spring so it sits in the grooves of the holder and lock its hook fully. A badly seated element lets dirt straight into the engine: run a finger round the edge to check it is seated evenly.
verification: Element seated evenly all round, hook or spring locked.

steps.title: Close up
steps.instruction: Refit the left side cover at 10 N·m.
verification: Lid (if fitted) and side cover back on and torqued.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write the date and hours on the service log and note anything unusual you saw (dirt past the filter, oil or water in the drain).
verification: Service logged.

title: Change the engine oil and filter
completeness: Covers draining the oil, changing the filter, refitting the drain bolt with the correct torque, filling with the correct oil and checking the level through the window. The engine, gearbox and clutch share this oil, so there is no separate gearbox oil to change.

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: Pro Honda GN4 4-stroke oil or equivalent motorcycle oil, SAE 10W-30, API SJ or higher (not Energy/Resource Conserving), JASO T903 MA.

prerequisites: Fresh oil of the correct grade on hand.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil filter fitted backwards: severe engine damage. Check the OUT-SIDE mark faces out.
Milky oil or metal flakes in the oil: stop and find the cause before running the engine.
Oil level not between the window lines: correct it before riding.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. The oil is changed every 6 races (about 15.0 hours of riding) and the filter every 6 races (about 15.0 hours of riding); both are changed after the first break-in ride and the oil is also changed whenever the clutch discs and plates are replaced. Check the level every race (about 2.5 hours of riding).
verification: Date, hours and reason written down.

steps.title: Warm the oil
steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for 3 minutes so the oil drains well, then stop it.
verification: Engine idled and stopped.

steps.title: Stand the bike upright
steps.instruction: Hold the bike upright on level ground (not leaning on a side stand). Remove the engine guard. Put a drain pan under the engine. The oil and the exhaust are hot: wear gloves.
verification: Bike upright, pan in place.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filler cap, then the oil drain bolt and its sealing washer, and let the oil drain completely. Look at the oil as it drains for metal flakes or a milky colour.
verification: Oil drained.
Oil colour and any debris noted.

branches.label: Metal flakes or milky oil
branches.condition: Do not just refill and ride: milky oil means coolant is getting in and flakes mean something is wearing. Record what you found and get the engine checked before running it.

steps.title: Decide on the filter
steps.instruction: If the filter is due (or the oil looked dirty or this is the first change after break-in), change it now while the oil is out.
verification: Filter decision made.

branches.label: Change the filter
branches.condition: Filter due or oil dirty.

branches.label: Oil only
branches.condition: Filter not due and the oil looked normal.

steps.title: Take the old filter out
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover bolts, the cover and its O-ring, then pull out the filter and the spring behind it. Let the cavity drain.
verification: Cover, O-ring, filter and spring out.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.instruction: Put a little grease on the spring where it touches the filter and fit the spring into the new filter. Push the filter in with the "OUT-SIDE" mark facing out. A filter fitted backwards starves the engine of oil and will wreck it. Oil a new O-ring, fit it to the cover, and refit the cover and its bolts, tightening them evenly and firmly.
verification: Filter in the right way round, new O-ring, cover bolts tight.

steps.title: Refit the drain bolt
steps.instruction: Oil the threads and seating face of the drain bolt. Fit a new sealing washer, oiled, and tighten the bolt to 23 N·m.
verification: Drain bolt torqued with a new sealing washer.

steps.title: Fill with fresh oil
steps.instruction: Use Pro Honda GN4 4-stroke oil or equivalent motorcycle oil, SAE 10W-30, API SJ or higher (not Energy/Resource Conserving), JASO T903 MA. Pour in 1.05 L (1.11 US qt). If the filter was changed too, the engine takes a little more: top it up at the level check in the next step. Check the O-ring on the filler cap, replace it if it is cracked or flattened, and refit the cap.
verification: Correct oil added, filler cap on.

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for 3 minutes. Stop it, wait 3 minutes, hold the bike upright on level ground and look at the oil inspection window. The level must be between the lower and upper lines; if it is at or near the lower line, add oil up to the upper line and check again.
verification: Level between the lines in the window.

steps.title: Check for leaks and close up
steps.instruction: Look at the drain bolt and the filter cover for any seep. Refit the engine guard if it was removed.
verification: No leaks, guard back on.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used and quantity, and whether the filter was changed. Dispose of the old oil and filter properly.
verification: Service logged.

entry_state: Bike on level ground, engine able to idle.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the correct level, new filter if due, no leaks, service logged.

title: Check, top up or replace the coolant
completeness: Covers the pre-ride cooling system check, the level check, a top-up, a full drain and refill, and bleeding air out. Does not cover replacing the radiator, hoses or the water pump seal.

required_parts.name: Coolant
required_parts.purpose: Pro Honda HP Coolant or an equivalent good quality ethylene glycol antifreeze with corrosion inhibitors, 1:1 mixture with distilled water.

required_parts.name: Drain bolt sealing washer
required_parts.purpose: Always new when the drain bolt is removed.

critical_stop_conditions: Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine.
Steady leak from the water pump bleed hole, or oil coming out of it: stop and have the seal replaced.
Coolant loss bigger than normal between rides: find the leak before riding.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the coolant every race (about 2.5 hours of riding) and the whole cooling system every race (about 2.5 hours of riding). Replace the coolant every 2 years, or sooner if it is dirty or was topped up with plain water. Write down the date and why you are doing this.
verification: Date and reason written down.

steps.title: Let it cool completely
steps.instruction: Only work on a cold engine. Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine: hot coolant can spray out and burn you.
verification: Radiator cold to the touch.

steps.title: Check the cooling system
steps.instruction: Look for coolant leaks at the hoses, the radiators and the water pump. Squeeze each hose: replace any that are cracked, soft or swollen, and tighten or replace loose hose bands. Look at the bleed hole under the water pump while the engine runs: a little weeping is normal, a steady drip of coolant or any oil means a seal needs replacing. Take off the radiator grills and check the fins: straighten bent fins and clear mud with low pressure water or air.
verification: Hoses, bands, radiators and pump bleed hole checked.

branches.label: Leak or damaged part found
branches.condition: Fix the leaking hose, band, radiator or seal before changing or topping up the coolant; record what was found.

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Hold the bike upright on level ground. Remove the radiator shroud upper bolt so you can reach the cap, lay a thick rag over the cap and remove it slowly. The coolant must be up to the filler neck. A loss of 20–60 cm³ through the overflow hose is normal; if you lose more than that between checks, find the leak.
verification: Level seen at the filler neck or the shortfall noted.

branches.label: Only a top-up needed
branches.condition: Coolant clean and not due for replacement.

branches.label: Replace the coolant
branches.condition: Coolant due (2 years), dirty, or diluted with water.

steps.title: Top up
steps.instruction: Top up to the filler neck with Pro Honda HP Coolant or an equivalent good quality ethylene glycol antifreeze with corrosion inhibitors, mixed 1:1 mixture with distilled water. At the track you can use clean soft drinking water in an emergency, but replace it with proper coolant as soon as possible.
verification: Coolant at the filler neck.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Put a pan under the water pump cover. Remove the coolant drain bolt and its sealing washer from the water pump cover, take the radiator cap off and let the coolant run out. Lean the bike well over to the right and then to the left a few times so both radiators empty.
verification: Coolant drained from both radiators.

steps.title: Refit the drain bolt
steps.instruction: Hold the bike upright. Fit the drain bolt with a new sealing washer and tighten it firmly.
verification: Drain bolt in with a new sealing washer.

steps.title: Fill
steps.instruction: Fill slowly through the filler neck with Pro Honda HP Coolant or an equivalent good quality ethylene glycol antifreeze with corrosion inhibitors, mixed 1:1 mixture with distilled water. A full change takes about 1.04 L (1.10 US qt). Fill right up to the filler neck.
verification: System filled to the neck.

steps.title: Bleed out the air
steps.instruction: Rock the bike over to the right and the left several times to push trapped air out. If the level drops, add more and repeat until it stays at the filler neck.
verification: Level stays at the filler neck after rocking.

steps.title: Fit the cap and shroud bolt
steps.instruction: Fit the radiator cap securely: a cap that is not fully home loses coolant and the engine overheats. Refit the radiator shroud upper bolt at 5.2 N·m.
verification: Cap fully home, shroud bolt torqued.

steps.title: Run and recheck
steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it warm up and check for leaks at the drain bolt and hoses. Let it cool completely, then check the level again and top up to the filler neck if needed.
verification: No leaks, level correct after cooling.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, what was done (check, top-up or full change), the coolant used and anything you found. If the bike will stand in freezing weather without enough antifreeze, drain the system first.
verification: Service logged.

entry_state: Bike cold, upright on level ground.
exit_state: Cooling system checked, coolant at the filler neck with the correct mixture, cap secure, no leaks.
title: Check, top up or replace the coolant
completeness: Covers the pre-ride cooling system check, the level check, a top-up, a full drain and refill, and bleeding air out. Does not cover replacing the radiator, hoses or the water pump seal.

required_parts.name: Drain bolt sealing washer
required_parts.purpose: Always new when the drain bolt is removed.

title: Check or replace the spark plug
completeness: Covers getting to the plug by hanging the tank, removing, inspecting, gap-checking and fitting the plug. Does not cover ignition coil or wiring faults.

required_tools.name: Hose clamp for the tank breather

required_parts.name: Spark plug
required_parts.purpose: NGK SILMAR9A-9S if the old one is worn.

critical_stop_conditions: Dirt dropped into the plug hole: get it out before refitting the plug.
Fuel hose kinked or leaking after the tank goes back: fix before starting.
Never ride with a tank cushion rubber missing.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. Inspect the plug every race (about 2.5 hours of riding).
verification: Date and hours noted.

steps.title: Take off the seat and radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Remove the shroud bolts on both sides and lift both radiator shrouds away. Keep each bolt with its part; the upper and lower shroud bolts are different.
verification: Seat and both shrouds off, bolts kept by position.

steps.title: Free the fuel tank
steps.instruction: Pinch the tank breather hose closed with a hose clamp and pull it out of the steering stem. Remove the bolt at the back of the tank and the tank rear band, then lift the throttle cables out of the guide on the tank so nothing is strained when the tank moves.
verification: Breather hose clamped, rear band off, nothing caught on the tank.

steps.title: Hang the tank on the left side
steps.instruction: Lay a shop towel over the left frame rail. Lift the tank slowly and hang it to the left side of the frame on its strap. Do not let it hang from the fuel feed hose, and do not kink or twist that hose. The fuel line stays connected.
verification: Tank hanging on its strap, fuel hose not stretched or kinked.

steps.title: Clean around the plug
steps.instruction: Blow around the plug cap and the plug hole with compressed air before you pull anything, so no dirt can fall into the cylinder.
verification: Area around the plug clean.

steps.title: Take the plug out
steps.instruction: Pull the plug cap straight off and unscrew the plug with a plug wrench.
verification: Plug out, hole covered with a clean rag.

steps.title: Inspect the plug
steps.instruction: Look at the centre electrode for wear, at both electrodes for carbon or dirt, and at the insulator for cracks. Note the colour. Check the gap with a wire-type feeler gauge only: if a 1.0 mm wire gauge goes into the gap, the plug is worn out. This is an iridium plug: never clean the electrodes and never bend the gap.
verification: Electrodes, insulator and gap checked.

branches.label: Plug worn, fouled or damaged
branches.condition: Gauge goes in, electrodes worn or dirty, or insulator damaged.

branches.label: Plug good
branches.condition: Gauge does not go in and the plug looks clean and undamaged.

steps.title: Get the correct new plug
steps.instruction: Use only the specified plug: NGK SILMAR9A-9S. Do not adjust its gap.
verification: Correct new plug ready.

steps.title: Fit the plug
steps.instruction: Screw the plug in by hand until it seats, then tighten it to 22 N·m with the plug wrench. Push the cap on until it seats.
verification: Plug torqued, cap fully on.

steps.title: Refit the tank, shrouds and seat
steps.instruction: Lift the tank back onto the frame, check the cushion rubbers are in place under it (never ride with one missing: fuel can leak), refit the rear band and bolt, route the hose and cables back into their guides and unclamp the breather hose, then push it back into the steering stem. Refit the shrouds: upper shroud bolts 5.2 N·m, lower shroud bolts 10 N·m. Refit the seat at 10 N·m.
verification: Tank seated on its cushion rubbers, breather unclamped and routed, shrouds and seat torqued.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Start the engine to check it runs cleanly. Write down the plug condition and whether it was replaced.
verification: Engine runs, result logged.

entry_state: Engine cold, bike on a stand, tank, seat and shrouds on.
exit_state: All valve clearances in spec, head cover and caps sealed and torqued, tank and bodywork refitted, readings logged.
title: Check and adjust the valve clearances
completeness: Covers getting to the head, setting top dead centre, measuring every clearance, changing shims through camshaft removal, the decompressor check, and closing up with every torque. Does not cover valve, seat or cam chain replacement.

required_tools.name: Tensioner stopper or holder tool for the cam chain tensioner lifter
Hose clamp for the tank breather

required_parts.name: Sealing washers for the short camshaft holder bolts, the head sealing bolt and the tensioner lifter bolt

prerequisites: Shim sizes on hand or available.
critical_stop_conditions: Anything dropped into the cam chain tunnel: get it out before turning the engine.
Calculated shim thicker than 3.000 mm: stop, the valve or seat needs work.
Decompressor weight not returning by itself: stop and have it checked.
Marks not lining up after reassembly: do not start the engine.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the valve clearances every 6 races (about 15.0 hours of riding) and after the first break-in ride. Write down the date, hours and any symptom (hard starting, popping, loss of power). The engine must be cold: below 35°C (95°F).
verification: Date, hours, symptoms written down; engine cold.

steps.title: Take off the seat and radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Remove the shroud bolts on both sides and lift both radiator shrouds away. Keep each bolt with its part; the upper and lower shroud bolts are different.
verification: Seat and both shrouds off, bolts kept by position.

steps.title: Free the fuel tank
steps.instruction: Pinch the tank breather hose closed with a hose clamp and pull it out of the steering stem. Remove the bolt at the back of the tank and the tank rear band, then lift the throttle cables out of the guide on the tank so nothing is strained when the tank moves.
verification: Breather hose clamped, rear band off, nothing caught on the tank.

steps.title: Hang the tank on the left side
steps.instruction: Lay a shop towel over the left frame rail. Lift the tank slowly and hang it to the left side of the frame on its strap. Do not let it hang from the fuel feed hose, and do not kink or twist that hose. The fuel line stays connected.
verification: Tank hanging on its strap, fuel hose not stretched or kinked.

steps.title: Clean the top of the engine
steps.instruction: Blow the cylinder head area clean with compressed air so no dirt can get into the plug hole or under the head cover.
verification: Head area clean.

steps.title: Open the head
steps.instruction: Pull off the plug cap and remove the spark plug. Disconnect the crankcase breather hose. Unplug the ignition coil connectors, remove the coil bolts and lift the coil out. Remove the head cover bolts with their mounting rubbers and lift the head cover off. Take the head cover gasket out of the cover.
verification: Plug out, head cover off, gasket kept clean.

steps.title: Open the inspection caps
steps.instruction: Remove the crankshaft hole cap and the timing hole cap from the left crankcase cover, with their O-rings.
verification: Caps out.

steps.title: Set top dead centre on compression
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a socket on the flywheel nut until the index line on the flywheel lines up with the index mark on the left crankcase cover. The timing marks on both cam sprockets must line up with the cylinder head mating surface. Look at the decompressor weight: if it is on the wrong side the piston is at the top of the exhaust stroke, so turn the crankshaft one more full turn counterclockwise and line up the marks again.
verification: Marks aligned, decompressor weight shows the compression stroke.

steps.title: Measure the clearances
steps.instruction: Slide feeler gauges between each rocker arm slipper and its cam lobe. Intake: 0.10 ± 0.03 mm. Exhaust: 0.20 ± 0.03 mm. Write down every reading, valve by valve. Do not dig the gauge into the rocker arms.
verification: Every valve measured and written down.

branches.label: All valves in spec
branches.condition: Every intake reading within 0.10 ± 0.03 mm and every exhaust reading within 0.20 ± 0.03 mm.

branches.label: One or more out of spec
branches.condition: Any reading outside its range: change the shims for those valves.

steps.title: Take the camshaft out
steps.instruction: Check again that the flywheel index line, the cam sprocket marks and the decompressor weight are on the compression stroke. Remove the muffler. Remove the cam chain guide B bolts and the guide. Remove the cam chain tensioner lifter bolt and sealing washer, fit a tensioner holder tool, turn it fully clockwise and lock the lifter. Remove the cylinder head sealing bolt and washer on the exhaust side. Loosen the camshaft holder bolts and the rocker arm shaft stopper bolt evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps, remove them with their sealing washers and lift off the camshaft holder (keep its O-ring and dowel). Lift the cam chain off the sprockets, take out both camshafts and hang the chain on wire so it cannot fall into the crankcase. Lift the rocker arms to reach the shims.
verification: Camshaft out, cam chain tied up, nothing dropped into the engine.

steps.title: Take out the shims of the tight or loose valves
steps.instruction: Lift out the shims of the valves you are adjusting with tweezers or a magnet. Mark each shim so it goes back to its own valve. Wipe the oil off each shim and measure its thickness with a micrometer.
verification: Shims out, marked and measured.

steps.title: Work out the new shim sizes
steps.instruction: For each valve: new shim = (measured clearance − specified clearance) + old shim thickness. Shims come from 1.200 mm to 3.000 mm in 0.025 mm steps; pick the nearest size and measure the new shim with the micrometer before fitting it. If the sum comes out thicker than 3.000 mm, carbon on the valve seat is the likely cause and the head needs proper valve work instead.
verification: New shim size worked out and measured for each valve.

branches.label: Calculated shim over 3.000 mm
branches.condition: Stop: the valve seat or valve needs attention; do not run the engine.

steps.title: Fit the new shims
steps.instruction: Fit each new shim on its own valve.
verification: Each shim on its correct valve.

steps.title: Check the decompressor
steps.instruction: Move the decompressor weight with your finger and let it go: it must spring back to its rest position by itself. If it sticks or the spring feels weak, the decompressor needs to be stripped and checked before the engine is run.
verification: Decompressor weight returns on its own.

steps.title: Refit the camshaft
steps.instruction: Lower the rocker arms. Oil the cam lobes, journals and thrust faces with molybdenum oil solution. Fit the exhaust camshaft with the decompressor weight facing down, fit the cam chain over both sprockets with their timing marks level with the head mating surface, and check the lobes are positioned for the compression stroke. Fit a new oiled O-ring to the camshaft holder, check the dowels, and fit the holder. Oil the bolt threads and seats, fit the long and short camshaft holder bolts (new sealing washers on the short ones) and the rocker arm shaft stopper bolt, and tighten them in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps to 13 N·m. Fit the cylinder head sealing bolt with a new sealing washer and locking agent on its threads at 14 N·m. Refit the tensioner lifter bolt with a new sealing washer, tightened firmly, and remove the tensioner holder. Refit cam chain guide B with its arrow facing forward at 9 N·m. Refit the muffler.
verification: Camshaft holder torqued, tensioner released.

steps.title: Recheck the clearances
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise several full turns to seat the shims, set top dead centre on compression again and measure every clearance again.
verification: All clearances now in spec.

branches.label: Still out of spec
branches.condition: Repeat the shim change for the valves still out.

steps.title: Refit the inspection caps
steps.instruction: Fit new oiled O-rings to the timing hole cap and the crankshaft hole cap and grease their threads. Tighten the timing hole cap to 6 N·m and the crankshaft hole cap to 15 N·m.
verification: Caps torqued with new O-rings.

steps.title: Refit the head cover
steps.instruction: Check the head cover gasket and replace it if damaged. Put liquid gasket sealant on the semicircular cut-outs of the cylinder head and fit the gasket to the cover. Refit the cover, fit the mounting rubbers with their "UP" marks up and tighten the head cover bolts to 10 N·m. Refit the ignition coil and its connectors and reconnect the breather hose.
verification: Head cover torqued, gasket seated, breather reconnected.

steps.title: Refit the plug
steps.instruction: Screw the spark plug in by hand, then tighten it to 22 N·m. Push the plug cap on.
verification: Plug torqued, cap on.

steps.title: Refit the tank, shrouds and seat
steps.instruction: Lift the tank back onto the frame, check the cushion rubbers are in place under it (never ride with one missing: fuel can leak), refit the rear band and bolt, route the hose and cables back into their guides and unclamp the breather hose, then push it back into the steering stem. Refit the shrouds: upper shroud bolts 5.2 N·m, lower shroud bolts 10 N·m. Refit the seat at 10 N·m.
verification: Tank seated on its cushion rubbers, breather unclamped and routed, shrouds and seat torqued.

steps.title: Start and check
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check it idles evenly with no oil leaks at the head cover or caps.
verification: Engine idles, no leaks.

steps.title: Record the readings
steps.instruction: Write down every clearance as found, every shim change (old and new thickness) and the final clearances. A valve that keeps closing up between checks is wearing and needs attention.
verification: Readings and shim changes logged.

entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine cold for any pack work.
exit_state: Clutch adjusted; pack measured and rebuilt if it was opened; oil refilled; no slip or drag.
title: Check and adjust the clutch, inspect the clutch pack
completeness: Covers lever free play with both adjusters, the test ride, and opening the clutch to measure discs, plates and springs and rebuild the pack with the spring bolt torque. Does not cover clutch basket or hub work.
excluded: Clutch basket, hub or primary gear work

required_parts.name: Clutch cover O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Always new when the cover is removed.

prerequisites: Oil change parts on hand if the pack is opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Correct free play cannot be set with both adjusters: inspect the clutch before riding.
Any part past its service limit: replace it (springs as a set, discs and plates as a set).
Oil leak at the clutch cover after the run: fix before riding.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the clutch system every race (about 2.5 hours of riding). Write down any symptom: slipping, dragging or a lever with too much or too little play.
verification: Symptoms written down.

steps.title: Measure the lever free play
steps.instruction: Measure the free play at the end of the clutch lever: it should be 10–20 mm (3/8 - 13/16 in).
verification: Free play measured.

branches.label: Free play in range
branches.condition: Free play 10–20 mm (3/8 - 13/16 in).

steps.title: Small adjustment at the lever
steps.instruction: Turn the cable end adjuster at the lever: one way adds free play, the other takes it away. If the adjuster is screwed out near its limit, screw it back in until it seats lightly and make the change with the in-line cable adjuster instead.
verification: Free play set or adjuster returned.

steps.title: Bigger adjustment on the cable
steps.instruction: Loosen the lock nut on the in-line cable adjuster, turn the adjuster to set the free play, then hold it and tighten the lock nut firmly. Recheck at the lever.
verification: Free play 10–20 mm (3/8 - 13/16 in), lock nut tight.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Test ride: the clutch must not slip under hard acceleration or drag when the lever is pulled. If you cannot get the right free play with both adjusters, or it still slips, open the clutch and inspect it.
verification: Clutch tested.

branches.label: Inspect the clutch pack
branches.condition: Slipping, dragging, or free play cannot be set.

branches.label: Clutch fine
branches.condition: No slip or drag.

steps.title: Drain the oil and open the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Drain the engine oil (see the oil change guide). Loosen the clutch cover bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps, mark where each bolt came from (they are different lengths), and take off the cover and its O-ring.
verification: Oil drained, cover off, bolt positions marked.

steps.title: Take out the clutch pack
steps.instruction: Loosen the clutch spring bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps and remove them with their washers, the springs and the pressure plate. Take out the lifter piece and the lifter rod. Lift out the friction discs and plates one at a time and lay them out in the order they came out, followed by the judder spring and its seat.
verification: Pack out and laid out in order.

steps.title: Measure the parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction disc thickness: standard 2.92–3.08 mm (0.115 - 0.121 in), replace at 2.85 mm (0.112 in). Check each steel plate on a surface plate with a feeler gauge: replace at 0.10 mm (0.004 in) warp. Measure each spring free length: standard 53.13 mm (2.092 in), replace at 52.23 mm (2.056 in). Look at the pressure plate, lifter piece, lifter rod, judder spring and seat for scoring, wear or damage. Springs are replaced as a set, and discs and plates are replaced as a set.
verification: Every disc, plate and spring measured and written down.

steps.title: Rebuild the pack
steps.instruction: Fit the spring seat and the judder spring the right way round (as they came out). Coat the friction disc linings with engine oil. Refit the discs and plates in the same order and direction they came out, starting with the first friction disc and then alternating plate and disc. Slide the lifter rod into the mainshaft and check it moves the lifter arm. Oil the bearing face of the lifter piece and fit it. Fit the pressure plate, the springs and the spring bolts with their washers, and tighten the bolts in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps to 12 N·m.
verification: Pack rebuilt in order, spring bolts torqued.

steps.title: Refit the cover and refill
steps.instruction: Fit a new oiled O-ring to the clutch cover, refit the cover and its bolts in their marked places and tighten them evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps. Refill the engine with fresh oil and check the level (see the oil change guide). If the discs and plates were replaced, the oil must be new.
verification: Cover on, oil at the correct level.

steps.title: Run and test
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check for oil leaks at the clutch cover. Test ride: no slip, no drag. Reset the lever free play.
verification: No leaks, clutch works.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the measurements, what was replaced, and the fluid or free play setting.
verification: Logged.

entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine cold for any pack work.
exit_state: Clutch adjusted; pack measured and rebuilt if it was opened; oil refilled; no slip or drag.

verification: Free play 10–20 mm (3/8 - 13/16 in), lock nut tight.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Test ride: the clutch must not slip under hard acceleration or drag when the lever is pulled. If you cannot get the right free play with both adjusters, or it still slips, open the clutch and inspect it.
verification: Clutch tested.

branches.label: Inspect the clutch pack
branches.condition: Slipping, dragging, or free play cannot be set.

branches.label: Clutch fine
branches.condition: No slip or drag.

steps.title: Drain the oil and open the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Drain the engine oil (see the oil change guide). Loosen the clutch cover bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps, mark where each bolt came from (they are different lengths), and take off the cover and its O-ring.
verification: Oil drained, cover off, bolt positions marked.

steps.title: Take out the clutch pack
steps.instruction: Loosen the clutch spring bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps and remove them with their washers, the springs and the pressure plate. Take out the lifter piece and the lifter rod. Lift out the friction discs and plates one at a time and lay them out in the order they came out, followed by the judder spring and its seat.
verification: Pack out and laid out in order.

steps.title: Measure the parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction disc thickness: standard 2.92–3.08 mm (0.115 - 0.121 in), replace at 2.85 mm (0.112 in). Check each steel plate on a surface plate with a feeler gauge: replace at 0.10 mm (0.004 in) warp. Measure each spring free length: standard 53.13 mm (2.092 in), replace at 52.23 mm (2.056 in). Look at the pressure plate, lifter piece, lifter rod, judder spring and seat for scoring, wear or damage. Springs are replaced as a set, and discs and plates are replaced as a set.
verification: Every disc, plate and spring measured and written down.

steps.title: Rebuild the pack
steps.instruction: Fit the spring seat and the judder spring the right way round (as they came out). Coat the friction disc linings with engine oil. Refit the discs and plates in the same order and direction they came out, starting with the first friction disc and then alternating plate and disc. Slide the lifter rod into the mainshaft and check it moves the lifter arm. Oil the bearing face of the lifter piece and fit it. Fit the pressure plate, the springs and the spring bolts with their washers, and tighten the bolts in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps to 12 N·m.
verification: Pack rebuilt in order, spring bolts torqued.

steps.title: Refit the cover and refill
steps.instruction: Fit a new oiled O-ring to the clutch cover, refit the cover and its bolts in their marked places and tighten them evenly in a crisscross pattern in two or three steps. Refill the engine with fresh oil and check the level (see the oil change guide). If the discs and plates were replaced, the oil must be new.
verification: Cover on, oil at the correct level.

steps.title: Run and test
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check for oil leaks at the clutch cover. Test ride: no slip, no drag. Reset the lever free play.
verification: No leaks, clutch works.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the measurements, what was replaced, and the fluid or free play setting.
verification: Logged.
